topStories.headline: Sherrill Wins District 2 in a Landslide, Securing His First Full Term
topStories.dek: The incumbent supervisor carried more than 84 percent of first-choice votes Tuesday, turning what had looked like a symbolic rubber-stamp into one of the most lopsided Board of Supervisors results in recent memory.
topStories.body:
Supervisor Stephen Sherrill won Tuesday's District 2 race with 84 percent of first-choice ballots cast, according to unofficial results released by the San Francisco Department of Elections on November 4. After ranked-choice elimination, his final tally reached roughly 91 percent of votes counted — an 82-percentage-point margin over his closest remaining challenger, Monthanus Ratanapakdee.

Sherrill had first entered office in late 2024 when former Mayor London Breed appointed him to fill the seat vacated by Catherine Stefani, who had won a State Assembly seat. He then prevailed in a June 2026 special election against Lori Brooke, the Cow Hollow Association president, by a 70-30 margin. Tuesday's general election, contested against Ratanapakdee, Nicholas Berg, and Guy McCoy, delivered a verdict that leaves little ambiguity about where District 2 voters stand.

The district covers the Marina, Pacific Heights, Cow Hollow, and Presidio Heights — neighborhoods that have been central to contentious debates over housing density, including the ongoing fight over the proposed Marina Safeway redevelopment. Sherrill has aligned himself with Mayor Daniel Lurie's moderate coalition, and Mission Local noted that all three moderate incumbents running Tuesday — Sherrill in D2, Alan Wong in D4, and Matt Dorsey in D6 — prevailed, preserving the Board's moderate majority.

Full unofficial results are posted at sfelections.org.

topStories.headline: Opponents File Federal Lawsuit to Block Marina Safeway Towers — Developer Seeks Dismissal
topStories.dek: A newly formed nonprofit and four Marina residents sued Align Real Estate in federal court over the 848-unit housing proposal; the developer's lawyers last week asked a judge to throw the case out.
topStories.body:
The legal fight over the proposed redevelopment of the Marina District Safeway has moved into federal court. A lawsuit filed by the YesAnd Foundation, Neighborhoods United San Francisco, and four Marina residents targets developer Align Real Estate, the City of San Francisco, its Planning and Public Health Departments, PG&E, and Safeway parent company Albertsons. The case was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California.

The plaintiffs contend that the project does not qualify for fast-track approval under state housing streamlining laws and that city planners approved it without adequate community input. Their complaint reaches for an unusual legal hook: Section 1983 of the Civil Rights Act of 1871, a Reconstruction-era statute. Last week, Align's lawyers asked the court to dismiss the suit, calling the tactic an abuse of a law originally designed to protect Black Americans from Klan violence, according to reporting by HousingWire.

The project itself calls for replacing the 1950s-era Safeway at 15 Marina Boulevard with two residential towers — 22 and 18 stories �� rising above a rebuilt ground-floor grocery store. Updated plans filed in July 2026 put the total at 848 apartments, including 86 units deed-restricted for lower-income households. The site, bounded by Marina Boulevard, Laguna, North Point, and Buchanan Streets, is currently zoned for 40 feet.

The lawsuit is the latest escalation in a months-long campaign. More than 300 residents packed a community meeting in July, and the Marina Community Association has repeatedly sent letters to Albertsons expressing opposition. The SF Chronicle reported in August that the Planning Department had already cleared a key eligibility hurdle, allowing the project to continue under state law despite Supervisor Sherrill's earlier attempt to halt it.

topStories.headline: City Calls Marina and Pacific Heights Families to a Listening Session This Saturday
topStories.dek: San Francisco's first citywide Community Needs Assessment comes to District 2 on November 7, with free food and childcare at Marina Middle School.
topStories.body:
The City and County of San Francisco is holding the District 2 leg of its "This Is Your City: 2026 Family Listening Series" this Saturday, November 7, from 11 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. at Marina Middle School, 3500 Fillmore Street.

The event is part of a 14-summit series organized by the city's Our Children Our Families Initiative (OCOFI) as part of San Francisco's first formal Citywide Community Needs Assessment. City officials are asking families, caregivers, young people, and residents to share their experiences and priorities so the city can direct services and programs accordingly. The District 2 summit covers Marina, Cow Hollow, Pacific Heights, Presidio Heights, and several adjacent neighborhoods.

Attendance is free and open to all San Francisco residents, not just District 2 households. Free food and childcare will be provided. Interpretation services are available for those who request them at least 48 hours in advance. Supervisor Stephen Sherrill is listed as a co-host on the city's event page.

moreNews.headline: Marina Yacht Harbor Channel Open After Dredging; Next Dredge Pushed to Fall 2027
moreNews.body: The SF Recreation and Parks Department's November 5 weekly update for the Marina Small Craft Harbor reports the main channel is open but advises boaters to navigate with caution, particularly near the north entrance side at low tide where sand continues to shift. The channel currently measures approximately 75 feet wide at a tide height of 6.9 feet. With the fall 2026 dredging cycle now complete and conditions stabilized, the harbor does not expect its next dredge until fall 2027. The harbor publishes channel-sounding updates every Thursday at sfrecpark.org.
